chunks: Follow the sequence in wudu (ablution) as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: begin with the face, then the hands, then wipe the head and the feet. Do not put anything before another in a way that opposes what you have been commanded.

So if you washed the forearm before the face, then begin with the face and repeat on the forearm. And if you wiped the foot before the head, then wipe over the head and then repeat on the foot. Begin with what Allah began with.

key_terms.الذِّرَاعَ: the forearm/arm, mentioned in the case of performing the washing out of order
key_terms.الرِّجْلَ: the foot, mentioned in the case of wiping before the head
key_terms.الْوَجْهِ: the face, the first part to be washed in the prescribed order
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification being discussed
key_terms.الْيَدَيْنِ: the two hands, washed after the face in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.بِالرَّأْسِ: the head, which is to be wiped after washing
key_terms.وَالرِّجْلَيْنِ: the feet, wiped in sequence after the head

ai.seo_question: What is the correct order of wudu (ablution), and what should be done if the sequence is broken?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on maintaining the prescribed order of wudu (ablution). It instructs that the face comes first, then the hands, then wiping the head and the feet, and that if the order is broken, the affected later act must be repeated after restoring the proper sequence.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.89 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:
"Follow the sequence of wudu as Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has commanded.
Start with the face, then the hands, then wipe the head and the feet. Do not precede anything before what you are commanded.

If you wash the arm before the face, start with the face and then repeat on the arm. If you wipe the foot before the head, then wipe the head and then repeat on the foot.
Begin with what Allah (swt) has started with."
Similarly, in the adhan to Salat and the iqamah, start with the first (shahada) and then the second (shahada) and so forth.
If you say: ‘Hasten to prayer (Hayya allas’Salat)’ before the testimonies, then you will again start with the testimonies and then repeat ‘Hasten to prayer.’"
